learning_outcomes.text: Know and distinguish types of companies by their main characteristics (sector, legal form, size, etc.), as well as different forms of business organization and identify their interaction with the environment.
Study the economic-financial viability of a project or investment and its impact on the social environment.
Perform economic-financial analyses of companies based on accounting data and calculate costs of a product or service.
Be able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.
Be able to become aware of the multidisciplinary nature of industrial engineering, as well as its social, economic, and environmental implications.

syllabus_topics: The generic environment of the company
The specific environment of the company
The interrelation between the company and other economic agents
Nature and objectives of business research
Development of productive processes and products
The relationship between innovation and business competitiveness
The innovation system in the European Union
assessment_rules: Students who do not pass during the course, in either ordinary or extraordinary calls, will be examined on the entire subject. The exam will consist of three parts: test, theory, and practical, with practical cases based on work developed during the course. For presentations or role-play activities, it is mandatory to perform them with a formal appearance; students not complying will not be evaluated for that activity. For continuous assessment to be taken into account, a minimum of 3.5 must be obtained in the final exam grade.
